blocks.text: An evidence rule defines where DSPM stores samples of sensitive data discovered during on-premises scans. You can configure DSPM to upload evidence data directly to your own cloud storage bucket, or allow DSPM to create and manage a storage bucket in your account. To learn more, see About Evidence Settings.

blocks.item: An on-premises data center is configured in DSPM.
A cloud storage bucket is available in your cloud storage account to store the evidence data.
1. Provide the general information.
From the navigation menu, go to Data Security > DSPM > Evidence Settings.
On the Evidence Settings page, click Add Evidence Rule.
See image.
The Add Evidence Rule page appears.
On the General Information tab, enter the following details:
Rule Name: Enter a name for the evidence rule.
Description (Optional): Enter a brief description for the evidence rule.
See image.
Click Next.
2. Select the cloud type.
On the Cloud Type tab, select the cloud provider for the evidence bucket.
See image.
Click Next.
3. Configure the storage option.
On the Storage Type tab, for the Storage Information section, select a storage option and provide the required details:
Custom Bucket: Use an existing bucket in your cloud environment.
S3 Bucket Name: Enter the name of an existing S3 bucket.
S3 Bucket Account ID: Enter the AWS account ID associated with the S3 bucket.
KMS Key ARN: Enter the ARN of the KMS key used to encrypt the evidence data in the S3 bucket.
Zscaler Managed Bucket: Allow DSPM to create and manage a storage bucket in your cloud account.
Account ID: Enter the AWS account ID in which you'll deploy the template.
For the IAM Role section:
IAM Role Name: Enter a name for the IAM role to be created in your AWS account.
A default name is prefilled. If needed, rename it to align with your organization's naming conventions. This role grants DSPM the necessary permissions to access the evidence bucket.
See image.
Click Next.
4. Select the on-premises data centers.
On the Data Center Association tab:
Data Center: Select the on-premises data centers to associate with this evidence rule.
See image.
Click Next.
5. Download and run the template.
On the Apply Changes tab:
Template Type: Select the template format to use:
CloudFormation
Terraform
Download Template: Click Evidence to download the template.
See image.
Run the downloaded template in your AWS account to grant DSPM the necessary permissions to access the evidence bucket.
Click Done.

blocks.text: The evidence rule is created, enabled by default, and appears on the Evidence Settings page. After creating the rule, validate the rule to verify that the template deployment is successful. After it is validated, and the evidence rule is set to enabled, DSPM uses this rule to upload evidence data from the associated on-premises data centers to the configured cloud storage bucket. To learn more, see Managing Evidence Rules.
